HTML-first build and acceptance

Build a coherent academic prototype in stages, with source files the frontend developer can restyle. The first deliverable is HTML design, not a complete production frontend or backend. A stage can share components with later stages; it must not rely on unbuilt optional features.

Deliverable contract

Create prototype/index.html, editable prototype/styles.css and prototype/app.js, plus fixture modules or embedded data as needed. Provide an offline bundle named prototype/Whiteboard-Academic-Prototype.html for review. Hash-style routing is acceptable for local HTML; preserve the W route semantics in a route manifest so later framework migration is straightforward. Do not overwrite the specification's REPORT.html or included original prototype.

Prefer a small router, shared shell, semantic components, domain records and pure rendering boundaries over one giant duplicated page per state. Keep CSS tokens independent so visual refinement does not rewrite grade logic. No build framework is required for the first HTML. If a receiving developer chooses tooling, record it and keep a readable offline artifact; dependencies must not make the design impossible to open.

Load local fixtures, no production endpoints. A scenario toolbar can select student/instructor/TA, course and error state. It belongs outside the product shell. A new role renders only permitted data. Clearly label the artifact “Prototype - fictional data.” Scenario storage may be local and resettable; it is not a secure grade system.

Every clickable app control must navigate, mutate sample state correctly, open a specified dialog or explain its bounded prototype limitation. Do not use a generic success toast for an unimplemented consequential action. Give local sample downloads real content and honest labels; do not claim they reached another system.

Build stages

StagePages and integrated outcomeExit check
0. FoundationW01-W06, W10, W13 and reusable shell/fixturesRole/course context, deep-link returns, session/permission states, light/dark and keyboard navigation work.
1. Teaching transactionW14-W24, W35-W40, W43-W44, W48-W49, W51-W53; bounded roster fixtureInstructor publishes one assignment; student selects/reviews/submits; TA reviews assigned work; instructor previews/releases; learner sees the right receipt and grade. Invalid and interrupted cases recover.
2. Assessment depthW25-W27, W41-W42, W45-W47, W50, W54, W57Quiz immutable attempts, timing/allowances, TA scope/expiry, rubric/manual override protection, groups, grading allocation and correction all connect.
3. Daily course lifeW07-W09, W11-W12, W28-W34, W55-W56Announcements, discussion, course/private calendars, reminders, activity, tools and help connect to the same course records. No private calendar leakage.
4. Course continuityW58-W60 and full W06 archive behaviorAttendance/insights use facts, copy/import excludes learner records, previews invalidate, prior term access is truthful.

Optional, separately selectedO01-O03Awards/assistant cannot alter grades or expose hidden context and cannot block a required journey.

The page catalogue's priority describes functional importance; the stage table describes dependency-aware implementation order. Some core pages need a bounded version in Stage 1 and deeper variants later. Keep a checklist of fields/states still outstanding; never call a page complete because its default screenshot exists.

Acceptance matrix

For each page ID record source path, implemented controls, states tested, desktop/narrow screenshots when permitted, keyboard result, assistive-technology result where run, issues and owner design feedback. Keep these statuses separate: specified, HTML implemented, source checked, browser checked, accessibility reviewed, owner accepted. A source check never sets the other statuses to Passed.

Mandatory scenario checks

  1. Wrong account/institution cannot accept an invitation; valid repeated acceptance does not add a duplicate course role.
  2. An unpublished or prerequisite-locked material is not accessible through search or a copied link; permitted availability text is clear.
  3. File upload rejects a corrupt/unsupported/oversized example, preserves the other files, and retries without duplicate submission. Keyboard selection/reordering has equivalent controls.
  4. Closing review or toggling offline produces no receipt. Successful send creates one exact received attempt with person/group, files/pages, accepted time and reference.
  5. Starting another attempt preserves the old receipt; later assignment/quiz edits do not change submitted contents.
  6. All required questions must be reviewed before marking grading complete. A manual rubric override survives a bulk rule update.
  7. Changing recipient scope, score, comment, attempt or policy makes release preview stale. TA deep-link/action attempts to release are denied.
  8. Aisha's fixture learner/staff totals equal 84.50% / 85.17%. Held results never leak into W24, search, notifications or exports available to that learner.
  9. Invalid policy weights, duplicate item mapping, empty categories, zero-denominator and overlapping letter ranges show actionable errors; no NaN/Infinity grade appears.
  10. A group member's accepted attempt creates one group receipt with captured members; a later membership change preserves it. Individual grade override clearly names the affected learner.
  11. Grading allocations drive both TA queue and calendar. Revoking/expiring access blocks current saves, preserving attributed prior work without exposing other scopes.
  12. Published announcements appear in course and activity at the selected time. Drafts do not. Read state does not delete the announcement.
  13. A private work shift remains private across role switches. Moving/cancelling a course event updates both calendar views and supersedes its earlier reminder.
  14. Grade correction preserves prior release, shows old/new and reason, and changes the learner only after re-release. No direct-message inbox is invented.
  15. A copied course contains zero learners/grades/submissions. Import blockers remain inspectable; changing mapping invalidates the accepted preview.
  16. Reset a scenario twice and repeat the journey; state starts consistently and does not mix prior users, terms or attempts.

Visual and accessibility review

Review representative desktop widths, 768px and narrow 320/390px layouts; long labels and multiple data rows; 200% text and 400% browser zoom where appropriate; light/dark; keyboard-only; reduced motion; high contrast/forced colors; a relevant screen reader in the permitted environment. Test focus after modal close, save failure, navigation and dynamically revealed errors. Test timer announcements, contained tables and full text alternatives. Record exact browser/OS/AT versions and what actually ran.

First HTML does not need every device-native capability, real push/email, a camera capture service or live SSO. It does need accurate denied/unavailable states and usable alternatives. Do not interpret prototype success as storage correctness, security assurance, accessibility certification or institution acceptance.

Later frontend integration boundary

After visual approval, the frontend developer may map semantic routes/components to their chosen stack. Agree on API/data contracts for identity/course scope, conditional writes/version conflicts, pagination/filtering, upload acknowledgment, quiz time authority, immutable attempt/release records, permission failures and notification delivery. Design a service adapter boundary in the frontend; do not couple UI to global fixtures everywhere. Real records and authorization require a separately approved engineering plan.

No backend provider, database, hosting, AI vendor, first school or SIS/IdP is selected by this handoff. SSO/LTI/import labels remain neutral until an institutional partner confirms them.
